text:
IncidentBot: Pager -> SLO breach p99 for customer `sienna` in us-west-2 detected by latency probe (streaming tail). p95 also creeping up. Auto-escalation to on-call: maya.

Maya: seeing the alert, joining now. can someone dump route/host info?

Sanjay: svc routing shows ~87% of requests hitting cluster gw-west-2a (dedicated pool for sienna). No obvious scaling events.

Alec: logs show a lot of long tail streaming stalls: repeated `recv_timeout` from the runtime layer. stack traces point to blocked IO while fetching KV cache pages.

Maya: customer impact? Jen can you confirm from CS side if tenants are reporting errors?

Jen: Sienna reported degraded streaming UX ~ 10m ago. Their frontend shows intermittent stalls and long partial responses. They say p99 jumps then recovers. They have a scheduled spike test later today (but that wouldn't explain the current immediate spikes).

OpsBot: Autoscaler status: pool-sienna-west-2 currently at 12/12 nodes, no recent scale-up due to saturation threshold not hit. CPU usage moderate, GPU mem > 70% on 3 nodes.

Maya: hypothesis: single-tenant long prefixes + high concurrency causing KV cache thrash + some requests get stall while waiting on remote kvcache fetch. Alec, can you confirm kvcache hit rate?

Alec: kvcache metrics for pool-sienna-west-2 last 15m: hit_rate dropped from 94% to 61% around 6234567680. Eviction rate spiked. Pattern: many unique long-prefixes during the window.

Sanjay: also seeing network retransmits to remote cache backend at ~6234567705. Could be small window of transient packet loss between hosts in AZ-a.

Maya: immediate mitigations: 1) route a portion of traffic to secondary pool (gw-west-2b) 2) lift per-customer concurrency limits temporarily 3) enable kvcache opportunistic prefetch for long-prefix paths. Let's pick two to act on now.

Alec: I can flip routing for 20% traffic to gw-west-2b using rollout policy `sienna-quick-shift`. Command:
```
# shift 20% to pool gw-west-2b
./rdctl rollout create --customer sienna --policy sienna-quick-shift --percent 20
```

Sanjay: lifting per-customer hard concurrency from 200 -> 260 for 10m to see if head-of-line queuing improves. I'll watch node saturation.

Maya: Jen, please tell Sienna we're routing a portion of traffic to a different pool and monitoring. Ask them for any reproducer prompts if they can.

Jen: messaging sent: "We're routing some traffic to a secondary pool and investigating streaming stalls. If you have the prompt set that caused spikes, please share." Sienna replied: "We ran an A/B prompt burst test at 09:13 that might be related, sending logs now."

IncidentBot: Change detected: rollout `sienna-quick-shift` started by Alec at 6234567920.

Alec: rollout completed to 20% at 6234567930. Early indicators: p99 on shifted subset is stable, overall p99 dropping ~18%. kvcache hit rate on target pool staying ~92%.

Sanjay: after increasing concurrency, CPU/GPU on original pool rose by ~5% but no overload. Queue depths less spiky.

Maya: good. continue monitoring for 15m. If p99 doesn't recover to within SLO, plan B is to failover more traffic and schedule a transient cache warming job.

Kyra: I noticed a subset of requests include very long single-token prefixes due to a client-side bug (repeated delimiter) — pushing a small sanitization filter to drop pathological prefixes might reduce unique cache keys.

Alec: can you post the filter snippet?

Kyra: 
```
# sanitize incoming prefix
if len(prefix_tokens) > 1024:
  prefix_tokens = prefix_tokens[:1024]
  // log truncated_prefix tag
```

Maya: let's not deploy filters mid-incident unless necessary. Logging truncation event for now.

Jen: Sienna sent their logs: a spike of concurrent sessions ~2.1x baseline triggered by their internal test. They confirm one test client was sending long repetitive delimiters. They will throttle their test.

Maya: action summary so far: 1) 20% traffic shifted to gw-west-2b (Alec) 2) concurrency limit lifted to 260 temporarily (Sanjay) 3) customer agreed to throttle internal test (Jen) 4) flagged kvcache warming + sanitization for follow-up.

IncidentBot: SLO status update: p95 back within target at 6234567960, p99 improving but still 1.6x SLO.

Alec: recommendation: run a short cache-warm job to prepopulate common prefixes on original pool, then gradually shift traffic back. I can prepare warm job with `--sample-from=sienna-recent` dataset.

Maya: do it. Alec, start cache-warm at low priority. Ops, keep autoscaler thresholds unchanged for now.

Alec: warming started at 6234567975. Sample size ~ 10k prefixes; estimated run 2m.

OpsBot: Warming job moved ~8k keys into local kvcache per node in first minute. Eviction rate decreasing.

Maya: monitoring shows p99 dropped to 1.05x SLO at 6234567988. Good trend.

Jen: Sienna confirmed improved UX after we routed traffic and they throttled tests: "Thanks, things look normal now."

Maya: We'll keep this thread open for 30m post-restoration for follow-up. Post-incident actions: - add a client-side guidance note on safe test harness behavior - consider kvcache soft-limits to avoid thrash - add a canary for repetitive-delimiter patterns.

Alec: filing follow-up ticket: INF-7834 "Sienna: kvcache thrash due to long repetitive prefixes; add client guidance + server-side heuristics".

Maya: closing handoff to ops for monitoring. On-call: Maya -> Kyra for next 30m.

Kyra: acknowledged, will watch for regressions.

IncidentBot: Thread marked resolved at 6234567999 (p99 within SLO).
